impressions.text: Delivered the issue #11 task `learnings submit|show|report` for shared model-learning logs — fork-based orchestrator submission with central numeric identity-to-project bindings, a trusted-base pull_request_target learning-label workflow, and seed import of 13 vmethod records plus 26 vecs rows — in a 34-file (+2315/−17) change that merged at its full 8-point estimate after two rounds.

Model strength: the codexbal/gpt-6.1-sol worker repeatedly stopped and escalated rather than bypassing boundaries, refusing to infer identity-to-project trust bindings from account names, flagging the missing seed-source read route and the unapproved label write permission, and declining to relabel invented data as recorded fixtures.

It protected data fidelity by correcting a stale count to import all 13 valid vmethod grade records and 26 PR-numbered vecs rows, omitting the single no-PR housekeeping row, and inventing neither a missing PR 357 row nor structured causes/findings from prose.

Weaknesses surfaced in review: round 1 requested changes on a blocking stale-fork defect (missing merge-upstream sync before Git database writes could 422 against newer central heads), unreadable report output with unrounded floats, premature outsider rejection in check-pr, and misleading show fallback wording, all resolved in round 2 with regression-before-fix evidence (11 failed/16 passed pre-fix) and a green 41-file/509-test suite.

Reporting was transparent: it disclosed a smoke-setup timeout under concurrent heavyweight checks (3007 ms against a 3000 ms budget) then passed all 505 tests on rerun without weakening timeouts, assertions or permission guards, and it declined to claim the live fork/PR write-smoke that remained the orchestrator's post-merge step.
